# Running the book {#sec-rebuild}

Everything is in
[`book/`](https://github.com/mdsumner/r-variants/tree/main/book) of
mdsumner/r-variants. A render runs each script in `book/scripts` under
both builds of R and writes the tables. Nothing is cached between renders.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `scripts/NN-name.R` | one example each; runnable alone with `Rscript` |
| `scripts/_bench.R` | the measuring helper the scripts share |
| `R/book.R` | runs a script under each build and makes the tables |
| `results/*.csv` | the rows from the last successful run of each script |
| `results/*.log` | each script's output per build (not committed) |
| `docker/Dockerfile` | the book image |
| `run.sh` | the render command |
| `pawsey/render.slurm` | the same, as a Slurm job for Setonix |

## The image

`ghcr.io/mdsumner/r-variants:book` starts from the published
`array-subset` image, which has patched R-devel in `/opt/R/variant`. It
adds stock R-devel in `/opt/R/baseline`, built from the same R-devel
commit the patched image records, so the two builds differ by the patch
and nothing else. The same altarr (`exp/r-hook`) and zaro are installed
into each, and Quarto. The **book** workflow in the repository builds the
image, renders the book in it as a test, and publishes it when asked
(Actions, **book**, **Run workflow**, `publish`).

The same workflow can publish the book it rendered to GitHub Pages: tick
`pages` when running it. That needs Pages set to "GitHub Actions" as its
source, once, in the repository's settings.

To move the book to a newer R-devel, rebuild and publish the
`array-subset` variant first, then the book image. The preface prints
what each build is.

## On Pawsey (Setonix)

Compute nodes on Setonix can reach the internet, which is why the book
runs there: the live chapters read from Copernicus, NCI and GitHub during
the job.

Once:

```sh
cd $MYSCRATCH
git clone https://github.com/mdsumner/r-variants
```

Each run, from the top of the clone:

```sh
git pull
sbatch --account=$PAWSEY_PROJECT book/pawsey/render.slurm
```

The job pulls the image to `$MYSCRATCH/altarr-book/book.sif` the first
time, renders, and leaves the book in `book/_book/` and the result rows
in `book/results/`. Its log is `altarr-book-<jobid>.log` where you
submitted. To keep a run, commit the result rows:

```sh
git add book/results/*.csv && git commit -m "Book results, Setonix, $(date +%F)"
```

Settings, all optional, passed with `sbatch --export=ALL,NAME=value`:

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `BOOK_MODE` | `live` | `offline` skips the scripts that need the network |
| `BOOK_PULL` | unset | `1` pulls the image again (after it is rebuilt) |
| `BOOK_MAX_CON` | `8` | connection cap for the Copernicus and EOPF chapters |
| `BOOK_THREDDS_CON` | `4` | connection cap for reads from NCI THREDDS |
| `BOOK_TRIES`, `BOOK_RETRY_WAIT` | `3`, `60` | attempts at a read that fails, and seconds between them |
| `BOOK_PAUSE` | `60` | seconds between the two builds on a live script |
| `BOOK_LATENCY` | `0.05` | seconds per fetch call in the simulated stores |
| `BOOK_SIF` | `$MYSCRATCH/altarr-book/book.sif` | where the image is kept |
| `BOOK_SINGULARITY_MODULE` | `singularity/4.1.0-slurm` | check with `module avail singularity` |

To render one chapter, pass it after the mode:

```sh
sbatch --account=$PAWSEY_PROJECT book/pawsey/render.slurm live 04-virtual.qmd
```

## Anywhere with Docker

On a laptop, a Nimbus instance or any machine with Docker, from the top
of a clone:

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work/book \
  ghcr.io/mdsumner/r-variants:book bash run.sh            # live
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work/book \
  ghcr.io/mdsumner/r-variants:book bash run.sh offline    # no network
```

## One script, by hand

Inside the image, from `book/`:

```sh
/opt/R/baseline/bin/Rscript scripts/04-virtual.R     # stock R-devel
/opt/R/variant/bin/Rscript  scripts/04-virtual.R     # patched
```

Outside the image the scripts run with any R that has altarr and zaro;
point `BOOK_R_STOCK` and `BOOK_R_PATCHED` at two `Rscript` binaries to
render the book against other builds.

## Adding an example

1. Write `scripts/NN-name.R`: source `_bench.R`, open a lazy array, wrap
   each read in `bench("label", x, expr)`, end with `finish()`.
2. In a chapter, show it with a `file:` chunk and run it with
   `book_run("NN-name.R", live = TRUE)` then `book_table(res)`.
3. Keep files ASCII.
